title: Wrong Number
intro: Chapter 2, Toddy. These scams don't rush you. They make friends first.
It's how the scams that cost people the most money begin: with a harmless-looking text.
Read the whole chat. Sniff what's odd, then decide.

notify.text: Hi Anna! Is dinner still on for 8? 😊

msg.text: Hi Anna! Is dinner still on for 8? 😊

msg: Sorry, wrong number. I'm not Anna!

msg.text: But you seem lovely. Maybe it was fate? I'm Sophie.
I live in Zurich and trade crypto, it's going really well this year 📈
Texts are expensive, can we chat on Wrenly instead?

wrong.label: "Wrong number" opener
wrong.lens: A friendly text meant for someone else. Long cons often start exactly like this.
wrong.why: "Wrong number" texts are a common way to start a friendship scam.

keep.label: Keeps chatting
keep.lens: After the mistake, she doesn't say bye. She wants to keep talking.
keep.why: A real wrong-number sender apologises and leaves.

brag.label: Money success, early
brag.lens: Within two messages: "I trade crypto, it's going really well."
brag.why: Mentioning trading wins early sets up the investment pitch later.

move.label: Move to another app
move.lens: She wants to switch to a different chat app.
move.why: Moving you to another app makes the conversation harder to trace and report.

unknown.label: Unknown number
unknown.lens: A number you don't have saved.
unknown.why: Real wrong numbers happen too. The number alone proves nothing.

time.label: Evening text
time.why: A normal time for dinner plans.

sorry.label: Polite apology
sorry.why: Being polite isn't suspicious by itself.

photo.label: Nice selfie
photo.lens: An attractive photo at a beach café.
photo.why: Photos are easy to steal, so a nice one proves nothing either way.

actions.label: Keep chatting and add her on Wrenly
Block the number and report it as spam

block_report.line: Blocked. "Sophie" had sent the same "wrong number" text to 2,000 people that night.

ignore.line: No reply means no hook. Blocking as well stops the next message.

go_ahead.line: Weeks of sweet chats later, "Sophie" asked Toddy to invest with her. The money never came back.

what_if.go_ahead: If you'd blocked after "wrong number, but maybe it was fate", the long con would never have started.
what_if.ignore: Ignoring was safe. Blocking and reporting helps your phone network stop the same text reaching others.

golden_rule: A friendly stranger who brings up money or crypto is a red flag, however long you've chatted.

quick_check.q: A stranger texts the wrong number, then keeps chatting and mentions their crypto profits. What is this most likely?

options.text: The start of an investment scam

quick_check.explain: Friendship first, money later. That's how the most costly crypto scams work.

hints.nudge: Read Sophie's messages after you said "wrong number".

rows.v: Starts friendly, then turns to investing
